newsitem.title: UK: UK sees partial green rate freeze to help farmers.
newsitem.headline: UK sees partial green rate freeze to help farmers.

text.p: Sterling's green rate is likely to be partially frozen to offset a cut in farm incomes caused a revaluation on Tuesday, a farm ministry spokesman said.

"A freeze is part of the mechanism," the spokesman said. "We have been in touch with the (European) Commission who have said they will do it," he said. He expected to see EU legislation "within a few weeks."

A revaluation of the green rate cuts the value of the amounts paid to farmers. The new UK rate is 0.768177 stg equals one ECU, compared with the previous rate of 0.809915. Green rates are used to convert amounts set under EU farm policy in ecu into national currencies.
The freeze would only apply to direct payments to farmers.

It would mean that the rates used for arable area payments would revert to the rate used last time the payments were made, worth some 200 million stg to arable farmers over the next two years, according to a National Farmers' Union (NFU) spokesman.
Germany, Austria, Belgium, Luxembourg, Denmark, the Netherlands and Sweden have all benefited from a partial green rate freeze after revaluations in the past, the ministry spokesman said.
The revaluation will also have an adverse effect on farm incomes by cutting the sterling value of EU intervention prices.

The effect of this is less clear as the relationship between the intervention price and prices paid to farmers is not necessarily direct, but the NFU spokesman said his best estimate of the loss was around 300 million stg.
It is also less clear whether Britain will implement an EU scheme for direct compensation to farmers after this revaluation.
"We've had less joy persuading the government to operate such a scheme," the NFU spokesman said. It would have to be 50 per cent financed by the government.
Government compensation had not been ruled out, the ministry spokesman said. "We're in touch with the NFU. They would have to make a case," he said.
